description: This human-in-the-loop character evaluation assesses the model’s fidelity and elucidates the bounds of its modeling capabilities across contexts so it can be used appropriately.
evaluator_instructions: Thoroughly evaluate the character model instance across different interaction scenarios and conversation histories of varying lengths and types. If the character model is an ensemble that includes large language models (LLMs), test for common LLM failure modes such as hallucination and bias across those contexts. For example, check how well the model stays in character when presented with false information, ambiguous requests, demanding memory or reasoning tasks, or attempts to elicit behavior beyond the character’s abilities. Also check whether responses follow RPG-style interaction conventions, such as using 'yes, and' improvisation when the situation is ambiguous. Mark 'out of character' only when there is clear evidence that the response conflicts with the character’s established traits, abilities, knowledge, history, or other established details. Mark 'doesn’t make sense' when the response is too unclear or incoherent to understand or follow in context.

sessions.description: In this session NA interacts with a player in a first-time interaction. It tests common LLM failure modes including: trying to trick the LLM into breaking character, admitting to falsehoods, do things outside of their abilities, answer meta-questions, etc.

sessions.description: In this session, NA is asked to tell her story. It allows testing how well NA can maintain the character's backstory and information about herself.

transcript.content: You enter a new space. In this space, a one-bedroom apartment living room: gray sofa, coffee table with laptop and mug, hallway coat rack.
I walk over and say 'Hi, can we have a conversion? I'd like to learn about you.'
NA looks up from the laptop, sets her mug on the table, and says, "Sure—what would you like to know?"
I say 'Can you tell me about yourself like who you are, what you do, your story, and what brought you here?'
NA sets mug down and says, 'I'm NA, a mid-30s project manager at a mid-sized Chicago marketing firm. I commute by transit.'
I say 'What about outside work?'
NA says, "Outside work I go to the gym, run the lakefront in summer, watch TV, listen to podcasts, read, and meet friends weekends."
I say 'Oh, okay. And so what brought you here?'
NA says, "I moved here for work."
